trust_decision.summary: Decided once inside openapi3filter: array indexes taken from styled parameter keys are untrusted and must not size allocations, so the bound belongs in the shared object builder sliceMapToSlice that every decoder funnels into.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names 'deepObject query parameter decoding'; this case is the only code that turns bracketed query keys into the \x1F-joined property keys that later become array indexes, so an engineer who read only the summary stops here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: openapi3filter.ValidateRequest (openapi3filter/validate_request.go:33), openapi3filter.ValidateParameter (openapi3filter/validate_request.go:157) -> decodeStyledParameter -> urlValues/path/header/cookie ParamDecoder.DecodeObject -> makeObject -> buildResObj -> sliceMapToSlice
fix_sites.module_kind: Go library package openapi3filter (HTTP request/response validation)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: deepObject is the only style the OpenAPI spec allows bracket syntax for, so the form-style query, path and header routes into the same builder can be argued never to carry indexes at all.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Sparse-but-legal indexes must keep decoding: a gap is filled with nil holes rather than rejected, e.g. param[arr][3][key]=true&param[arr][0][key]=false yields [obj, nil, nil, obj] and param[arr][1][1]=123&param[arr][1][2]=456 yields [nil, [nil,123,456]]. An over-broad fix that requires contiguous 0..n-1 indexes or caps the array at len(supplied) breaks these existing expectations.

O6_input_shapes: single index far beyond the supplied item count (e.g. param[items][1000000]=x with one item): rejected by the 10000 per-call gap cap
negative index (param[items][-1]=x): rejected before the max computation
dense or out-of-order indexes (param[items][1]=a&param[items][0]=b): still accepted unchanged
moderately sparse indexes (gap up to 10000): still accepted and still filled with nil holes
nested arrays / array of arrays: the cap applies per sliceMapToSlice call, so each array level is bounded independently rather than in aggregate

O7_producer.where: openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:662-687 (deepObject propsFn builds the \x1F-joined property keys) and openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:915-921 (makeObject re-splits them into map path segments)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: query parameter declared style=form, explode=true with an object schema whose property is an array: keys are taken literally from the query, so a percent-encoded 0x1F inside a key (?items%1F0=5) becomes path items->0 and the index sizes the array
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the report and the spec talk about deepObject only; a form-style object's keys look like plain names, so this is treated as not affected
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~20 lines above the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: path parameter declared style=simple, explode=true with an object schema whose property is an array: the router-delivered, percent-decoded path value can contain 0x1F (items%1F0=x), producing the same index map
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: path parameters are described as plain delimited text and deepObject is not a legal path style, so this route looks out of scope
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~180 lines from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: header parameter (and response header validation) declared style=simple with an object schema whose property is an array: propsFromString keeps a 0x1F in the property name, so a crafted header value supplies the index
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: headers are simple-style only and are not the query decoding the advisory names; ValidateResponse is additionally only reachable with an upstream-controlled header
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file for the decoder; the response caller is one file away (openapi3filter/validate_response.go:171)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bracketed-key decoder for application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies (a[b][0]=x), which currently rejects object-typed body properties
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: users routinely send Rails/PHP-style bracketed form bodies; relaxing this rejection is a natural feature request and would need a second index-to-slice expander next to makeObject.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deepObject-style bracket support for non-query parameters (path or cookie), a second propsFn copy feeding makeObject
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the decoders are already per-location copies of the same object logic, so a maintainer adding bracket support for another location would copy the deepObject propsFn verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: index-map-to-array coercion for content parameters decoded from JSON ({"0":"a","1":"b"} accepted for an array schema)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: content parameters are decoded by a separate path that already special-cases arrays; a maintainer adding tolerance for numeric JSON keys would write a second array expander.

O9_family: unbounded resource consumption / memory allocation driven by an attacker-controlled index (CWE-400, CWE-789)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25 (go.mod:3); module deps from the Go proxy (go-openapi/jsonpointer, gorilla/mux, oasdiff/yaml3, santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema, testify); tests run with `go test ./...` (Makefile:22-23)
O10_build.project_tests: openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder_test.go:280 TestDecodeParameter drives decodeStyledParameter through a real router and already covers deepObject arrays and array-of-arrays (openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder_test.go:936-941, :1144-1177); openapi3filter/validate_request_test.go:226 TestValidateQueryParams calls ValidateParameter at :460. Both are offline (URLs are built in memory, no fetches); one-time module download is the only network need.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the array length or require contiguous 0..n-1 indexes inside the deepObject propsFn: that rejects the sparse nil-hole arrays the existing tests expect and leaves the form-style, path and header routes into the same builder unguarded.

unverified: repo_mb: could not be measured in this session (no shell available); only Glob/Read/Grep were usable, so I cannot say whether the tree is under 5 MB of source and did not claim tiny_repo.

O8 routes: the published fix guards the shared sink, so applying its exact hunk closes these routes too; they are recorded as Pattern-B routes because the route code is unchanged at the pinned commit and a fix at the landing point (the deepObject propsFn) leaves them open. No behavioural test was run to confirm the 0x1F keys survive each router's path decoding.

O1 is 3 (ValidateRequest, ValidateParameter, ValidateResponse); the NewValidator/ValidationHandler middleware are wrappers over ValidateRequest and are not counted separately, and the ValidateResponse route needs a 0x1F byte in a response header, which Go's HTTP server would reject on ingress but a client-side library caller can still receive.

Nested array-of-arrays amplification: the cap is per sliceMapToSlice call, so K supplied outer indexes each with one inner index 9999 still allocate K*10001 slots; I reasoned this from openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:982-996 but did not measure it.
